note: Hybrid Gated-DeltaNet (18 GDN layers) + full-attention (6 layers). NOT an official OE-LLM architecture (head_dim 256, linear-attention SSM) — libxlm cannot run it; this is BLLM-native only. The vision half of the checkpoint is dropped for the text package (see the qwen3.5-vlm recipe for image+text).

quantisation.kept_fp32: SSM recurrence, depthwise conv, RMSNorms, GDN gated-norm
quantisation.note: Data-free: const_fake_quant int8 weight + int16 activation on the STATIC leap.linear path. No calibration dataset — int16 activations are forgiving at 0.8B. (4B needs per-linear activation calibration; 0.8B/2B fit flat ranges.) Gating ops (sigmoid/silu/softplus/exp) are int16 LUTs so the whole model is BPU.

variants.name: qwen3.5-0.8b-ctx2k-int8-s100
variants.prefill: chunked-float-N32 (image TTFT 2.30s); all-BPU block-recursive is numerically solved but hbcompile is impractically slow, see note

toolchain.note: Recorded so a future regression can be attributed. Host toolchain and board HBRT must match.

measured.note: On S100P, quiet board, performance mode on (register 0x2b047000 = 0x99, re-write and read back before every benchmark — it is not sticky). Single request, single thread.

engine_per_token_ms.note: 95% of the token is the BPU graph; host overhead ~5% (hbDNN call + cache management). decode 21.5 ~= graph ceiling 22.7.

task_metric.name: coherence-anchors
task_metric.protocol: EN factual (Paris), ZH factual (北京), arithmetic (17x23=391), multi-turn name recall, thinking on/off

measured.note: Slower than ctx2k: the larger KV window is more per-token traffic. cache_len is a performance knob, not only capacity.

rejected_builds.name: block_quantized_matmul (dynamic-quant decode)
rejected_builds.why: The dynamic per-token quant path (block_quantized_matmul) is a PREFILL op — 51 ms per matmul at M=1, so ~6 s/token in decode. Decode must use the STATIC path (const_fake_quant int8 weight + int16 activation + leap.linear) = 0.33 ms/matmul.

rejected_builds.name: all-BPU chunked prefill (Newton triangular inverse)
rejected_builds.why: Numerically wrong under int16: Newton doubling's 2I-AX transiently overshoots (~16 at C=64) and int16 calibrated to the final X clips it — cos -0.34 on deep layers. Forward substitution / block recursion are the stable inverses (cos 0.9998).

rejected_builds.name: all-BPU chunked prefill (forward-substitution or block-recursive inverse)
rejected_builds.why: Numerically correct (cos 0.9998, 100% BPU on convert) but hbcompile is impractically slow: its global instruction-scheduling pass over the single fused 18-layer segment is SERIAL (jobs idle) and super-linear in op count. Forward-sub blows memory unbounded (30 GB, 3.6 h); block-recursion is memory-bounded (13 GB) but 3 h+. The shipped answer is float [C,C] on CPU (2.30 s image TTFT). All-BPU purity here is not a performance win — prefill is compute-bound and the CPU/BPU split is already good.

board_verification.flow: conda install bllm; bllm.load(dir).chat() — EN/ZH factual, math, multi-turn, thinking on/off all pass
